source.title: Hippocampal place-cell sequences depict future paths to remembered goals

confidence_rationale: Canonical, highly-cited (Nature, single-unit hippocampal recording) direct demonstration that hippocampal place-cell sequences encode prospective trajectories toward remembered goals -- the foundational empirical result the 2026 theta-sweep papers extend. Moderate transfer risk: rat, physical-space navigation, not abstract goal-directed cognition (REE's actual claim domain).
failure_signatures: The paper's own framing is limited to 'replay'-class sequence events in an open arena with learned reward locations -- it does not test whether the same mechanism operates for non-spatial or abstract goal structures, which is the generalisation MECH-236/MECH-289 (and the 2026-08-08 REE thought that prompted this pull) actually need.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Before goal-directed navigation in an open arena, rat hippocampal place-cell sequences ('replay' events) encode spatial trajectories strongly biased toward progressing from the animal's current location to a known goal location, predicting the animal's subsequent path even for novel start-goal combinations.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct empirical precedent for MECH-289's claim that the hippocampal trajectory generator actively generates novel-path sequences (not merely replaying executed paths), and for MECH-236's claim that hippocampal proposal generation must be goal-conditioned rather than purely positional -- this paper is the original demonstration that goal-directedness, not just novelty, characterises these sequences.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Physical spatial navigation in an open arena, not abstract/relational goal-directed cognition. Whether the same computational primitive generalises to REE's action-object space (SD-004) or an abstract possibility topology (SD-097) is the architectural hypothesis this evidence motivates but does not itself test -- see SD-098's own literature_evidence note for the same caveat applied to the follow-up 2026 papers.
mapping.source_context: Long-Evans rats, open-arena spatial memory task with multiple reward locations and a designated home goal; single-unit hippocampal place-cell recordings.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (canonical Nature paper, foundational to the entire theta-sweep/prospective-replay literature, >1000 citations). Mapping fidelity capped at moderate because REE's claims are about an action-object/abstract topology, not literal physical space -- the paper directly supports the narrower 'hippocampal sequences are goal-directed and generative' premise, not the broader abstract-generalisation hypothesis.
